summary: Contrastive RAG at temp 1.2 to surface tail questions
hypothesis: Raising temperature to 1.2 on the contrastive-RAG best base (exp011) should surface sharper, task-specific unknown questions that live in the tail of the distribution — the complementary upper endpoint to exp019's greedy floor.
technique: The exp011 contrastive few-shot RAG pipeline is run unchanged but with decoding temperature raised to 1.2 (vs. model default), sampling deeper into the tail to test whether high-temperature draws can unlock coverage-improving questions that greedy/default decoding misses.
result: Scored 0.267 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), a regression of −0.056 vs the exp011 best (0.323) and −0.040 vs baseline (0.307). Coverage stayed pinned at 3 with identical recurring gaps, while high temperature introduced atomicity/naturalness degradation and catastrophic context leakage (demo-bleed from the contrastive prompt), falsifying the tail hypothesis and closing the decoding lever entirely; discarded.
